text:
vikram: ran nsys+perfetto on the dedicated pool after last deploy. 95/99th for short seqs jumped ~2.5x. suspect batching-window fragmentation + lots of tiny kernel launches causing tail latency.
jen: which traces? link?
vikram: uploaded trimmed nsys export and a perfetto link. short TL;DR: many small matmul kernels and repeated host->gpu memcpy bursts aligned with queue flushes.
matt: can you paste the nsys command and a short kernel timeline snippet?
vikram: command used: 
```
nsys profile --output=run_2026-03-18 --trace=cuda,osrt -t cuda,kerneltime --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx
```
snippet from timeline (abridged):
```
00:00.000 memcopy H2D 2.2us
00:00.003 matmul_small_f32.launch 5.1us
00:00.010 memcopy H2D 1.8us
00:00.013 matmul_generic_v2.launch 12.4us
00:00.030 kernel-idle 100us
```
I can drop full trace in GCS if useful. perfetto link: https://perfetto.app/trace/abc123 (private)
sara: saw similar in last week's run — when continuous batching window < ~6ms we end up with micro-batches; launch overhead dominates for seqs < 64 tokens.
jen: any evidence the kernel selector fell back to the wrong kernel? e.g., choosing generic_matmul_v2 for sizes that should hit specialized path?
vikram: yes — selector logs show heuristic picked generic_matmul_v2 for dims around 48x48 after the selector threshold tweak. this increased average launch time and amplified queue churn.
matt: regression introduced in rollout f3f2d1? I remember a selector tweak landed recently.
vikram: bisected to commit 8c3f9af — changed adaptive_threshold from 32 -> 48 in the kernel selector (intended to reduce tiny-specializations), but sign/inequality logic bug made it the opposite effect.
sara: that explains it — more tensors routed to generic path. also noticed KV-prefill traffic spikes interleaving with micro-batches; cache-eviction/reserve timing looks correlated.
jen: proposed mitigations?
matt: short-term: bump continuous batching min_window_ms to 6ms on dedicated and prefer cache-prefill before releasing batch. also add a temporary rule: for tensors <64x64 prefer specialized_small_matmul.
vikram: long-term: add selector unit tests that exercise sequence-length distributions and a perf harness that simulates Poisson arrivals to surface batching-window fragmentation. I'll draft a perf test that emits random short seqs and measures 95/99th.
perf-bot: perf alert created: PERF-2026-118 — 95th latency regression in dedicated pool. linked run: run_2026-03-18
jen: action items:
- vikram: open PR to revert/patch selector bug + include unit tests (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- matt: deploy config tweak (min_window_ms=6, cache-prefill=true) to canary (ETA today)
- sara: add perf test harness + perf dashboard panel for micro-batch churn (ETA this week)
- perf-bot: attach trace artifacts to PERF-2026-118 ticket
vikram: will attach full nsys .qdrep and perfetto URL to the ticket. assigning @matt to the immediate config change.
jen: also add a small note to the runbook about interpreting these timelines: look for repeated memcopy+small-kernel pattern, and check selector decision logs and batching-window histograms.
sara: +1 :thumbsup:
